projectsMeta.coworkNote: These live in the cloud and can be set public or private. Cowork projects are separate: they sit locally on a person’s desktop and stay private to them, so the real total across Ashgrove Press is higher.
projectsMeta.sharedMeaning: "Shared" counts projects more than one person has actually opened, which is a stricter test than the public/private setting.

cost.explainer: Ashgrove Press pays a monthly fee for each seat. When someone goes past their plan limit, any further usage draws on a prepaid credit balance. Those are two separate charges, shown separately below.

subscription.note: The monthly bill for seats. This is the large majority of what Claude costs.

usage.note: Metered usage from 1 to 30 September, on top of the plan. Drawn from prepaid credits.

credits.note: Prepaid balance that absorbs usage spikes. Includes credits granted by Anthropic, so it is not all money Ashgrove Press has spent.
credits.autoReload: Tops up to £150 when the balance falls to £50

watch.title: September metered usage against August
watch.body: $897 between 1 and 30 September against $514 for the whole of August, both in US dollars from the same series. The current period resets on 1 October 2026.

watch.title: Two accounts are 57% of it
watch.body: Of the £705.91 billed, £209.39 and £191.21 are two people. 6 of 30 have any metered usage at all, so this is a small number of heavy workloads rather than a broad rise.

claudeCode.blockedReason: The per-user pull request and lines-of-code charts show “Data processing in progress”. The Claude Code GitHub app needs confirming on the Ashgrove Press repositories before per-engineer detail appears.

modelSpend.caveat: These are the charges for usage above plan limits, so this shows which models the overspill ran on. Everyday work inside a seat is free and sits outside these figures.
modelSpend.derivedNote: Each month is summed from the daily spend-by-model series, so every figure is read directly; nothing is derived from quarter or year-to-date totals.
